after: ## What the section asks of you
alt: Paper 3 is worth 50 marks, split equally between Section A Shakespeare and Section B Drama at 25 marks each. Section B is one essay on a modern non-Shakespeare play, assessed like Section A on AO1 to AO5 at 20% each. You choose an (a) essay on the whole play or a (b) printed passage, and the play is not allowed in the exam room.
caption: One essay on a modern play, worth 25 marks and assessed on all five objectives.

after: ## What the section asks of you
alt: Two overlapping lists of Section B plays. Nottage’s Sweat and Soyinka’s Kongi’s Harvest are set in both 2026 and 2027. O’Neill’s Long Day’s Journey Into Night is 2026 only, and Wertenbaker’s Our Country’s Good is 2027 only.
caption: Sweat and Kongi’s Harvest carry over; one play changes.

after: ## How this differs from Paper 1 drama
alt: The close-reading skills from Paper 1 still apply: stage directions as evidence, dialogue rhythm, dramatic irony and structure. Two things change: AO5 requires the argument to engage with and evaluate other interpretations, and knowing the modern theatrical conventions the plays use or resist becomes part of AO1 and AO2.
caption: Same close reading, plus AO5 and modern theatrical conventions.

alt: Four cards. Naturalism in Long Day’s Journey Into Night: life as lived, long stage directions, and fog that becomes symbolic. Time and structure in Sweat: scenes move between 2000 and 2008, creating structural dramatic irony. Ritual and music in Kongi’s Harvest: song, dance and crowd scenes, with satire. Metatheatre in Our Country’s Good: convicts and officers rehearse a play, and doubling sharpens class and power. A note on setting and space follows.
caption: Each set play uses, or resists, a different theatrical convention.

alt: Top: Long Day’s Journey Into Night as four acts running from morning to midnight on one day in August 1912, with the fog thickening across them. Bottom: Sweat drawn as scenes moving between a 2008 lane and a 2000 lane, so the audience sees consequences before causes and watches earlier scenes with structural dramatic irony.
caption: One play runs straight through a day; the other shows outcomes first.

alt: Three sources of alternative readings for modern plays. Production choices: casting, design, doubling and cuts. Critical approaches: a Marxist or economic reading of Sweat, a postcolonial reading of Kongi’s Harvest, a feminist reading of Mary Tyrone, and a reading questioning whether Our Country’s Good is too optimistic about theatre. Audience positions: first audiences and audiences now or in different countries. Each reading must be weighed, not listed.
caption: Production, criticism and audience all supply readings to weigh.

alt: A flow from the model paragraph on Long Day’s Journey Into Night. Structure: blame circulates through confessions shared among all four Tyrones. Two readings: Mary as centre and victim, or a feminist reading of the house as her prison. Tested against the text: the men get the longest final confessions and Mary enters only at the end. Judgement: everyone is both cause and casualty, so the ending offers recognition rather than resolution.
caption: Structure, two readings tested against the text, then a judgement.

alt: For a question on friendship in Sweat, a weak thesis says friendship is important and tested. A stronger thesis argues that Nottage stages friendship in a single shared bar that splits when Cynthia’s promotion divides her from Tracey, and that the 2008 outcome shadows every earlier scene of loyalty. It names a staging choice, uses the structure and gives a line to argue.
caption: A strong thesis argues about method: staging and structure, not just theme.
